dataset_description: Checked-in retrospective-style benchmark sample used to show how a less-synthetic collaborator pack can preserve the same reviewer-facing proof shape as the demo benchmark.
labeling_policy: This sample remains deidentified and intentionally bounded for repository use. Labels emphasize reviewer-visible pancreatic risk, actionable follow-up, and escalation cues rather than autonomous diagnostic claims.
notes: Repository sample for public proof only. This is not a clinical validation dataset.
notable_strengths: Three deidentified cohorts now share the same reviewer-facing casebook shape.
Highest-confidence positives still concentrate near the top of the review queue.
known_limitations: Sample remains small and deidentified for repository use.
One follow-up-only miss and one pancreatitis confounder overcall remain visible.

cohort_descriptions.description: Front-door abdomen CT intake cases that mix overt lesions, secondary-sign patterns, and negative controls.
Referral MRI workup cases with richer pancreatic follow-up cues and one intentional follow-up-only miss.
Navigator-style referral review cases that keep reviewer-facing excerpts and confounders visible in the same proof shape.

benchmark_bucket_descriptions.description: Reports with overt lesion or malignancy wording that should stay easy to justify in a reviewed queue.
Cases driven by ductal obstruction, atrophy, or related pancreatic risk cues without always naming a mass.
Cases where the operational signal is pancreatic follow-up or workup language rather than explicit malignancy wording.
Specificity checks where inflammatory language can look worrisome without supporting suspicious morphology.
Clearly nonsuspicious pancreatic reports that should stay out of the flagged worklist.
